title: NOAA CPC ENSO probabilities issued 2013-2026 were skilful but under-confident, as were the IRI model probabilities they follow; a past-data sharpening gave no score gain
abstract: Question: were the official NOAA CPC ENSO probability outlooks (La Nina, neutral, El Nino for nine overlapping seasons) calibrated, and what caused any error? Method: we collected 159 monthly issues (August 2013 - October 2026) from IRI Quick Look tables, digitised CPC charts (maximum error 0.5 points) and CPC RONI archive pages, and the objective CCSR/IRI model-based probabilities for the same months. A plan was written before scoring. The 150 ONI-era issues (1,349 forecasts) were verified against the current CPC ONI, with a cluster bootstrap over 12-month issue blocks. Results: the outlook was skilful (RPSS 0.49, 95% interval 0.32-0.61, against 1991-2020 climatology; 0.28, 0.05-0.42, against a damped-persistence regression trained on 1951-2012). It was under-confident, not over-confident: the best tempering q ~ p^b had b = 1.50 (1.11-2.05); categories forecast at 55-65% occurred 74% of the time, and categories forecast at 5-15% occurred 3.6%. The IRI objective probabilities had the same exponent (1.57, 1.22-2.08) on matched targets, while the 1951-2012 regression was calibrated (0.90, 0.66-1.32). The implied Gaussian width of the IRI forecasts was too large up to about six months lead (RMS standardised error 0.58 at leads 0-2, 0.76 at 3-5, 0.97 at 6-8). CPC follows IRI closely (CPC ~ IRI^0.89 climatology^0.11), and we found no clear human value added or lost. A sharpening estimated only from earlier years changed the RPS by -2.5% (-9.2% to +3.6%); the in-sample gain is only 2.3%, and sharpening failed in years when ENSO changed against the guidance (2016, 2024). Against ERSSTv5 ONI the La Nina total was calibrated (ratio 1.02); the current ONI revision makes it 1.20, and RONI 0.62, which shows the category change from the February 2026 switch to RONI. Limitations: about 13 independent years and few ENSO events, revised index values, eleven digitised issues, and too few RONI-era forecasts (36) for a calibration test.
